body.x: AnyAble, Ltd. (CEO Choi Dong Cheul) announced its participation in CES 2025, to be held from January 7 to 10 in Las Vegas. The company will present its cutting-edge 3D Printed Electronics (3DPE) printer and its research and development roadmap at the K-Startup Pavilion.

Established in September 2023 as a research-focused company, AnyAble was born from the technology transfer and equity investment by the Korea Electrotechnology Research Institute (KERI). Since then, the company has concentrated on advancing its 3DPE and biosensor technologies capabilities, aiming to become a global leader.

AnyAble plans to showcase its 3DPE printer internationally at CES 2025. The printer, which utilizes a conductive ink dispensing method, supports high-precision 3D printing at 100µm resolutions, making it versatile for applications across multiple industries.

By the end of this year, AnyAble aims to develop a 50µm-class 3DPE printer, which it plans to market to domestic and international professionals. To enhance its offerings, the company is also investing in developing bio-MEMS sensor chips using Solution Immersed Silicon (SIS), a semiconductor-based technology.

These Bio-MEMS sensor chips are designed to grant higher resolutions (100–50µm) to AnyAble's 3DPE printers, enabling the creation of complex 3D structures beyond traditional PCBs. The chips will also support diverse experimental conditions, ensuring flexibility and user convenience.
Additionally, AnyAble is expanding its product lineup to include industrial-grade and nanometer-scale 3DPE printers, further solidifying its leadership in the global 3DPE market.

An AnyAble representative explained, “With the demand for 3DPE technologies rising in advanced industries like semiconductors, there’s a lack of established brands or manufacturers leading this sector, apart from a few niche startups. CES 2025 provides us a strategic opportunity to showcase our technological capabilities, gather feedback from diverse international customers, and expand our market presence.”

The representative added, “While targeting the highly receptive North American and European markets, we plan to initially penetrate Southeast Asia, where market entry barriers are relatively lower. By supplying research-oriented products in this region, we aim to accelerate the commercialization process and eventually deliver high-quality solutions to global markets.”

AVING News, which has covered CES for 19 consecutive years, continues to bridge the gap for Korean SMEs and startups looking to expand globally. To promote Korean startups worldwide, AVING will host its Broadcasting Zone at the Venetian Expo, featuring the CES Media Day Startup Conference and global media interviews. AVING’s international media partners will cover these programs.
Following CES 2025, AVING will co-host review conferences with participating companies in Korea, offering a platform for increased visibility and improved corporate image.
